summary: US-F2: The sale charges passed-on fees and records the breakdown, per channel
description:
**As** a buyer, **I want** the fees I actually pay to be visible on what I am buying, **so that**
the total I am charged is explainable line by line — and **as** an organizer, **I want** the fees I
absorb recorded even though the buyer never sees them.

**Priority:** P0  **Depends on:** TKT-214

TKT-6's first COS: *every order line carries a fee breakdown; buyer-visible vs absorbed is correct
per channel*. This is the slice where fees become money.

**The trap this ticket exists to close:** `absorbed` and `passed_on` are not a display flag. A
passed-on fee increases what the card is charged; an absorbed fee does not, and yet must still be
recorded, because TKT-217 has to pay it to a payee out of money the buyer already paid. A build
that treats incidence as presentation charges the wrong total in one channel and cannot settle in
the other.

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- [ ] `ReservationCreate` accepts an optional channel code (opaque string, 1..100, ADR-024's exact
  shape). Absent = the default/public channel, which resolves NULL-channel fee rules only. The
  existing GA and seated request shapes stay valid — mind `minProperties`/`maxProperties`, which is
  how that schema expresses its XOR today.
- [ ] Commerce resolves fees through TKT-214's catalog read for the reserved ticket type **and
  channel**, with the same two failure classes the price path already distinguishes
  (`errResolveUnavailable` / `errResolveUnusable`). It **never degrades to "no fees"**: an
  unavailable or unusable fee resolution refuses the sale, exactly as an unusable price resolution
  does. "No rule matched" is a successful resolution with an empty fee set and must not be
  conflated with either failure.
- [ ] The breakdown is computed in **integers only** (ADR-001): per-ticket and per-order fixed
  bases, and a percentage base as basis points with **checked** multiplication and the rounding
  direction the TKT-214 ADR documents. No float anywhere on the path.
- [ ] `passed_on` fees increase the reservation's `total_amount`; `absorbed` fees do not change
  what the buyer pays. **Both** appear in the breakdown. A test proves two reservations differing
  only in channel — same base price, same fee amount, opposite incidence — charge different totals
  and record the same fee amount.
- [ ] The reservation persists a fee snapshot with the same discipline as
  `price_resolution_snapshot` (migration 0006): the resolution document **verbatim** plus the
  computed breakdown, snapshot-not-reference, the storability guard applied **before** the hold
  exists, nullable and not backfilled, with the shape pinned by a DB-level CHECK.
- [ ] The `Reservation` response carries the breakdown (per fee code: code, basis, incidence,
  amount, currency) and splits `amount` into face value and passed-on fees. It must be **optional**
  in the contract, not required — every pre-existing reservation response lacks it and ADR-028
  fails closed, so requiring it would turn valid responses into 500s. Regen committed.
- [ ] Any total that would exceed the contract's `Money` bound is refused **before** inventory
  commits — a 4xx, never a 500 with an orphan hold. The existing `quantity < 1 ||
  amount > MaxInt64/quantity` guard moves with the arithmetic, it does not get left behind on the
  price-only path.
- [ ] Checkout charges the reservation's stored `total_amount` unchanged. **Exactly one place**
  computes the fee — recomputing at capture is the divergence bug ADR-036 names for prices.
- [ ] `make check` green (lint + test + build, Go & TS, gateway smoke suite); regenerated code committed before the gate runs (ADR-009).

**Non-goals:** payees and splits (TKT-216) · the settlement ledger (TKT-217) · fee behaviour on
refund, exchange and cancellation (carved out to a follow-up; see the epic readiness verdict) ·
storefront display of the breakdown (the response carries it; rendering is TKT-2/TKT-17 work).

objective.note: A sale charges the right total per channel and records a fee breakdown that TKT-217 can settle from.

scope.note: Commerce only, reserve + checkout. Snapshot, breakdown, incidence, channel. No payees, no ledger, no post-purchase.

uncertainties.note: Whether per-order fixed fees are apportioned across lines or carried once on the reservation - today a reservation is one ticket type, so it may be moot; the plan states which and why. Rounding unit comes from TKT-214's ADR, not from this plan.

dependencies.note: Blocked by TKT-214: this ticket consumes its resolution contract and its ADR's rounding rule.

approach.note: Mirror services/commerce/internal/api/catalog_pricing.go end to end: one read, strict-semantics/tolerant-fields decode, storableSnapshot before the hold, validate() before use. Extend rather than fork - two near-identical consumer files is how one of them stops being maintained.

first_slice.note: The money path is the COS; everything else in the epic reads what it writes.

success.note: Charged-total assertions and snapshot-shape assertions; the incidence proof is a differential test across two channels.

binding.rule: Money is integer minor units + ISO currency code - floats are banned on money paths.

Local gate: `make check` (lint + test + build, Go & TS, plus the gateway smoke suite; run `make deps` first on a clean clone). CI runs the same gate - keep them mirrored. Commit regenerated code (`openapi_gen.go`, `api-types.gen.ts`) before running the gate - `check-generate` diffs against HEAD, so an uncommitted regen reads as drift and fails the run.

governingAdrs.why: SHIPPED BY TKT-214 AND THIS TICKET'S DIRECT INPUT. Fixes the fee model: three basis kinds as a database-enforced tagged union (per_ticket_fixed / per_order_fixed / percentage_bps), FLOOR rounding AT THE INDIVIDUAL TICKET with checked multiplication before the divide (§2 - this ticket implements that arithmetic; catalog never multiplies), passed_on vs absorbed incidence and what each does to the charged total (§3), exact-match channel semantics with NULL meaning channel-agnostic and an omitted channel NOT being a wildcard (§4), catalog-resolves/commerce-computes ownership with ADR-002 unamended (§5), the /internal/ read and its X-Internal-Token guard (§6), and - easy to miss - §2's rule that A RESOLVED FEE OF AMOUNT 0 IS STILL A RESOLVED FEE and must appear in the breakdown.

The pricing model ADR-046 extends. Relevant here for §2's integer-safety requirement and for the precedent that commerce consumes catalog's resolved number and NEVER recomputes it - two places computing one number is a divergence bug waiting for its first mismatch.
Money is integer minor units + ISO-4217. Every fee computation on this ticket is integer-only with a checked multiplication; no float, no big.Float, no decimal-as-string round trip.

Commerce owns 'pricing/fee/promo evaluation' - the arithmetic is this service's job. Catalog owns the rules. ADR-046 §5 deliberately did NOT move that line, so this ticket must not push arithmetic back into catalog.
Contract-first: ReservationCreate and Reservation changes must be declared in services/commerce/api/openapi.yaml and the generated code committed BEFORE the gate.

Response validation fails closed. A new REQUIRED response field turns every pre-existing valid response into a 500 - which is why the breakdown must be optional in the contract, exactly as Reservation.seats had to be.

The checkout journal protocol: what commerce may do before and after the hold exists. A failure AFTER inventory commits leaves an orphan hold and a 500 for the buyer, which is why TKT-153 moved the snapshot storability check to before the hold. Same discipline applies to the fee snapshot.
The claim runs in one Postgres transaction and is the correctness boundary. Nothing here may make the claim conditional on a second network read completing after the hold.

Checkout recovery REPLAYS a checkout whose outcome is unknown. A total recomputed on replay from a re-resolved fee set would drift from the total the buyer authorised; only the stored total may be charged.
Channel codes are exact opaque strings, 1..100 chars, NULL = default/public. Inventory already stores one on claims. There is no registry; do not invent one.

SAME-WEEK ADR, included by the TKT-214 retro rule rather than by area match - and it is the one that governs how commerce reaches catalog's new /internal/ route. Declared security: guards a service's PUBLIC contract; an inline check guards its internal surface. Commerce already holds catalog's internal token and calls /internal/ticket-types/{id} with it (server.go:1158, internal=true) - the fee read takes the SAME credential, so this adds no blast radius.
Same-week-adjacent: the PSP port boundary. The captured amount is what the provider confirmed; the fee breakdown must reconcile to it, not to a recomputation.

reference.summary: Epic lineage and the three epic-level COS
The fee model, shipped and merged - read §2 (rounding), §3 (incidence), §4 (channel), §9 (a considered code with a null winner)

The read this ticket consumes: GET /internal/ticket-types/{id}/fee-resolution?channel_code=... , X-Internal-Token, 401. Winner is NULLABLE - a code every rule of which is outside its window resolves with winner:null and must be skipped, not treated as a fee of zero
The consumer to mirror end to end: one read, strict-semantics/tolerant-fields decode, storableSnapshot BEFORE the hold, validate() before use, two failure classes that never degrade to a default
The reserve path, the EUR-only limitation, and how commerce sends the internal credential (call(..., internal=true))
The snapshot precedent: nullable, not backfilled, CHECK-shaped, Down refuses to drop with data present
ReservationCreate's minProperties/maxProperties XOR - adding an optional property changes those counts and the XOR must still hold
TKT-214 closeout: the two agent-made decisions this ticket inherits (the forced/channel inversion, and the /internal/ route)

comments.body:
<!-- sdlc:stage=ready kind=claim -->
### Claimed — TKT-215 (US-F2)

**Selection.** TKT-214 closed, which unblocked exactly two children: this one and TKT-216. Both have
zero open blockers now. Chose TKT-215 on **unblocking power** — TKT-217 needs both, but TKT-215 is
also what makes TKT-214's work reachable at all (nothing consumes fee rules until this ticket), so
it is the slice that converts a shipped-but-inert feature into a demonstrable one. Tie-break by
lowest key was not needed.

**Blockers verified:** `blocked-by TKT-214` — **resolved** (Done, merged `0d821677`). No other links.

**Branch:** `TKT-215-sale-charges-fees`, cut from `origin/main` at `d39ac330`.

**Risk verdict — `risk:low` NOT claimed.** This ticket changes **what a buyer is charged**. It is the
money path itself, not a model for it: a new request field on the sale, new arithmetic on the total,
a new persisted snapshot, and a migration in commerce. Three of `risk:low`'s carve-outs apply (money
path, data migration, >5 files). The plan gate would be mandatory under normal operation; it is
waived here only by the owner's blanket waiver for this epic, not because the ticket is small.

**Gates waived — same terms as TKT-214**, recorded again so this ticket's history stands alone:
Gate 1 given by the owner's instruction; Gate 2 replaced by agent judgement after the cross-model
critique (prefer the critique's recommendation, else the most reversible option, every decision
recorded in `kind=plan-final`); Gate 3 replaced by agent squash-merge after the ai-review converges
under the unchanged churn cap, review-guide posted first as the audit record; Gate 4 replaced by
self-validation of each COS against test evidence on merged code. Cross-model review, TDD with tests
observed red, `make check` green before every push and after the merge, and no AI attribution all
apply unchanged.

**Model routing**, re-read from `.claude/sdlc.config.json` at claim time — unchanged from TKT-214:
`plan` = `gpt-5.6-luna` · `planReview` = `main-agent` · `implement` = `main-agent` ·
`aiReview` = `gpt-5.6-luna`. Both cross-model pairs hold.

**Context-mémo RE-BAKED at claim, not merely revalidated.** The shaping-time bake was written before
ADR-046 existed, so its `governingAdrs` were a snapshot of a world without the model this ticket
consumes. Re-resolved against `docs/adr/` at HEAD:

- **ADR-046 added** — the ticket's direct input, and the source of the rounding rule, the incidence
  semantics and the nullable-winner case this implementation has to handle.
- **ADR-043 added** — and this is the TKT-214 retro applied to itself. That ticket's mémo missed
  ADR-043 because it was resolved *by area* and an auth-guard ADR does not look like "fee rules";
  it turned out to govern the ticket's most consequential decision. The retro's concrete change was
  *include every ADR dated within the current week regardless of area match*. Doing that here
  surfaced ADR-043 (2026-08-05) and ADR-032 immediately — ADR-043 is what says commerce may keep
  using the credential it already holds rather than needing a new one.
- Twelve governing ADRs in total, each with what it constrains **for this ticket**.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan -->
### Execution plan — TKT-215 (draft)

**Drafted by `gpt-5.6-luna` (Codex, read-only, effort=high)**, per `config.models.plan`. 122 tool
calls, worktree untouched. Condensed; every cited file/symbol was independently re-verified at HEAD
during plan-review.

#### 1. Arithmetic

`face_value = unit_face × quantity` · `total_amount = face_value + passed_on_total` ·
absorbed fees recorded but excluded from the buyer total.

Per basis: `per_ticket_fixed` = `amount × quantity` · `per_order_fixed` = once per reservation ·
`percentage_bps` = `floor(unit_face × rate_bps / 10000)` **per ticket, then × quantity** — matching
ADR-046 §2's worked example (150/150/100 at 333 bps → 4+4+3 = **11¢**, not the 12¢ of line rounding
or the 13¢ of order rounding).

Checked arithmetic required at five points: fixed × quantity · `unit_face × rate_bps` before the
divide · per-ticket result × quantity · fee subtotal accumulation · `face + passed_on`. The existing
`quantity < 1 || amount > MaxInt64/quantity` guard (`catalog_pricing.go:205`) moves into the composed
total, and the final total must also be `<= 9007199254740991`. All of it **before** the inventory
hold, answering 400.

A zero-valued winning fee stays in the breakdown (ADR-046 §2).

#### 2. Totals model and existing consumers

The draft enumerated every consumer, as asked:

| Consumer | Site | Draft's verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Reserve replay | `server.go:347` | replay stored total + breakdown, never re-resolve |
| Checkout load | `server.go:631` | reads fee-inclusive total |
| PSP charge | `server.go:1028` | charges stored gross unchanged |
| Order facts / journal | `server.go:674` | records gross |
| Recovery | `store/recovery.go:96` | stored gross, no re-resolution |
| **Exchange source** | `store/exchanges.go:159,194` | **"source totals will include passed-on fees, while target exchange pricing remains price-only… the known exchange-fee gap explicitly carved out of the epic; do not redesign exchange settlement here"** |
| Refunds | `store/refunds.go:176` | `q × unit_amount`; "passed-on fees therefore are not refunded yet" |
| Cancellation refunds | via the bulk runner | same gap |
| Staff conversions | `server.go:1163,1226` | stay price-only, nullable snapshot |

#### 3–4. DoD and files

`ReservationCreate.channel_code` optional 1..100, `maxProperties` 3 → 4 · fee resolution called with
the channel through `call(..., internal=true)` · unavailable/unusable refuse the sale, empty fees
succeed · null winners kept in provenance but produce no breakdown item · new commerce migration
`0014_fee_resolution_snapshot.sql`, nullable, not backfilled, shape CHECK, `Down` locks then refuses
· new response fields all **optional** (ADR-028 / the `seats` precedent) · extend
`catalog_pricing.go` rather than forking a second consumer · regenerate and commit before the gate.

#### 5. Test plan

Pure: per-ticket rounding on a `150,150,100 @ 333bps` fixture — *"a fixture with only one repeated
price cannot distinguish per-ticket from line/order rounding"* · each basis · mixed incidence · zero
winner · four overflow points.

Consumer (fake HTTP): exact-channel resolution asserting catalog receives `channel_code=reseller`
and that inventory receives **face** `unit_amount` not the gross · default channel excludes
channel-specific rules · fail-closed on six unusable shapes with the inventory fake asserting it was
**never called** · empty fee set succeeds · null winner neither errors nor becomes a zero fee · zero
winner retained beside a non-zero one · composed-total overflow refused before inventory.

PostgreSQL: snapshot nullable/not-backfilled/CHECK/rollback · replay returns the stored breakdown
after catalog rules change.

Smoke: two reservations differing only by channel — same face, same fee amount, **different totals**
· checkout charges the stored total after catalog rules are mutated · an old required-only
`Reservation` payload still validates.

#### 6–7. Risks and open decisions

Null winner as zero fee · zero treated as absent · overflow before the divide · snapshot stored
after the hold · replay recomputing · required response field · omitted channel as wildcard ·
channel normalisation · generated drift. Open: (1) whether a channel should reach **inventory**
allocation — recommends propagating to GA, leaving seated alone; (2) snapshot envelope field names;
(3) future multi-line `per_order_fixed`.

<!-- sdlc:stage=plan-review kind=plan -->
### Adversarial plan critique — TKT-215

**By `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)**, per `config.models.planReview`. Critic did not draft.

#### Seam verification at HEAD — clean

`catalog_pricing.go:81/108/205` · `server.go:128,347,631,674,1028,1163` · `store/recovery.go:96` ·
`store/exchanges.go:159,194` · `store/refunds.go:176` · migration `0006` · `openapi.yaml:209,255`
— **all exist and say what the draft says they say.** Next commerce migration is `0014` ✅. This is a
well-grounded draft; the problem with it is not its facts.

#### ⛔ A1 [blocking] — the draft's own Risks section refutes its Decision

This is the failure mode `quality-practices.md` §1 names: *every fact right, the synthesis wrong*.

The draft **correctly finds** that `ExchangeDelta(sourceTotal, targetTotal) = targetTotal − sourceTotal`
(`exchanges.go:126`), that `sourceTotal` comes from `reservations.total_amount` (`:159,194`), and
that `targetTotal = resolution.total(quantity)` is **price-only** (`api/exchanges.go:152,200`). It
then writes, in its own risk list:

> *"Exchange/refund/cancellation semantics silently assumed correct: leave those paths unchanged and
> document the known fee gap; `total_amount` now represents gross captured money, while post-purchase
> refund logic still derives face-only amounts."*

**That sentence refutes the plan it appears in.** Work the arithmetic:

    face 4550, passed-on fee 300  →  total_amount = 4850
    buyer exchanges for an identically-priced ticket
    targetTotal = 4550   sourceTotal = 4850
    delta = 4550 − 4850 = −300   →  settleExchangeDelta takes the `default:` branch
                                 →  a 300-cent PARTIAL REFUND, on an even exchange

The system spontaneously refunds the service fee on **every even exchange**, under-charges every
upgrade by the fee, and over-refunds every downgrade. That is money moving wrongly on a shipped
path, introduced by this ticket.

**It is not the carved-out gap.** TKT-6's readiness verdict carved out *whether fees are refunded* —
a product question. It did not carve out *breaking the exchange delta for any order that carries a
fee*. Calling an arithmetic break a "known gap" is how a defect ships wearing a waiver.

**Amendment.** Keep `total_amount` as the gross charge — the draft is right that charge
(`server.go:1028`), order facts and the payments journal (`:674,:684`) all want the money that
actually moved. But **add `face_value_amount` in the same migration and repoint the exchange source
queries at it**, in this ticket. Properties:

- legacy rows are correct **by construction** — backfill `face_value_amount = total_amount`, which is
  exactly true for every pre-fee reservation;
- exchanges resume comparing face-to-face, so behaviour is *unchanged* rather than newly correct;
- each site is then forced to say which number it means, which is the whole reason one column cannot
  serve both.

**Required test:** an even exchange on an order carrying a passed-on fee moves **zero** money. That
test fails against the draft as written.

#### ⛔ A2 [blocking] — `maxProperties: 4` silently breaks the GA/seated XOR

The draft says *"`minProperties` remains 3; `maxProperties` becomes 4"*. Enumerate what that admits
with five properties and two required:

| body | count | admitted? |
|---|---|---|
| `{org, tt, quantity}` | 3 | ✅ intended |
| `{org, tt, seats}` | 3 | ✅ intended |
| `{org, tt, quantity, channel}` | 4 | ✅ intended |
| `{org, tt, seats, channel}` | 4 | ✅ intended |
| **`{org, tt, quantity, seats}`** | **4** | **✅ — and it must not be** |

The schema's own description says the property counts are *how the XOR is expressed*. The draft's
change makes the contract stop expressing it. The handler enforces it independently, so this is not
exploitable — but that same description says a direct caller "must not be able to slip past the
schema", so a contract that no longer refuses it is a defect on the terms the document sets itself.

**Amendment.** Keep `maxProperties: 4` and add `not: {required: [quantity, seat_identities]}`.
One line, enforced by the request validator, and invisible to `oapi-codegen`'s struct generation, so
the generator objection that ruled out `oneOf` does not apply. **Required test:** a body carrying
`quantity` *and* `seat_identities` *and* `channel_code` is refused **by the contract**, asserted
through the spec router rather than the handler.

#### ⛔ A3 [blocking] — do not propagate the channel to inventory

Open decision 1 recommends passing the channel through to GA inventory holds. **Rejected**, and this
is a scope-and-blast-radius call rather than a taste one: inventory's `channel_code` is not a label,
it is what `channel_allocations` caps consumption against (ADR-024). Propagating it means a sale that
resolves a fee for `reseller` now **claims against the reseller allocation** — and starts being
refused with 409 when that allocation is exhausted, on ticket types nobody changed.

This ticket's COS is about **what the buyer is charged**, not about which pool the claim draws from.
Adding propagation later is additive; a sale that begins failing on an allocation cap is an incident.
TKT-176 already exists for channel-allocation semantics and is the right home.

**Resolve fees by channel; send no channel to inventory.** State it in the plan so the omission reads
as a decision rather than a miss.

#### Accepted

The arithmetic and its ADR-046 §2 derivation, including the per-ticket rounding fixture argument ·
the five checked-arithmetic points and the pre-hold placement · extending `catalog_pricing.go`
rather than forking · null-winner and zero-winner handling · all new response fields optional, with
the `seats` precedent · migration shape and `Down` guard · the fail-closed test matrix with the
inventory fake asserting it was never called · replay reading the snapshot · open decisions 2 and 3.

#### Rejected

Open decision 1 (channel → inventory), per A3.

#### Pre-mortem lens

*Assume the PR bounced.* (1) An exchange test goes red and the fix is a schema change → **A1**.
(2) A contract test admits both `quantity` and `seat_identities` → **A2**. (3) A smoke reserve starts
409-ing on an allocation cap → **A3**. (4) The gate's registry tests fire on a new Store method or a
declared header → run module tests before the gate (TKT-214's retro, already applied). (5) The
snapshot fails to store *after* the hold → the draft already places the guard before it.

Lens changed the plan in three places — A1, A2, A3.

<!-- sdlc:stage=planning kind=plan-final -->
### Plan final — TKT-215

**The `kind=plan` draft, as amended below, is the plan.** Delta only.

#### Amendments

**A1** `total_amount` stays gross, **and** `face_value_amount` is added in the same migration
(backfilled `= total_amount`, exactly true for every pre-fee row) with the two exchange-source
queries repointed at it. Test: an even exchange on a fee-carrying order moves zero money.
**A2** `maxProperties: 4` **plus** `not: {required: [quantity, seat_identities]}`. Test: the
contract itself refuses a body carrying both.
**A3** No channel propagation to inventory. Fees resolve by channel; the claim is unchanged.

#### Decisions made by the agent because Gate 2 is waived

Rule: prefer the critique's recommendation; where it makes none, take the most reversible option.

| # | Decision | Rule | Rationale |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | `total_amount` = gross; add `face_value_amount`; fix exchanges here | critique recommends | Charge, facts and journal want gross; exchange wants face. One column cannot mean both, and the draft's version moves money wrongly on an even exchange |
| D2 | Contract expresses the XOR via `not`, not by property count alone | critique recommends | The count trick cannot survive a fifth property; `not` is one line and the generator ignores it |
| D3 | No channel → inventory | critique recommends | Additive later; an allocation-cap 409 on an unchanged ticket type is an incident. TKT-176 owns it |
| D4 | Snapshot envelope: `resolution` (verbatim) + `breakdown` + `face_value` + `passed_on_fees` + `total_amount` | most reversible | Keeps catalog's document intact; TKT-217 reads the same envelope. Renaming later is a migration, so the shape is chosen to be additive |
| D5 | `per_order_fixed` applied once per reservation, amount **and** basis persisted | most reversible | Today a reservation is one ticket type, so per-order and per-line are indistinguishable; persisting the basis lets the future cart ticket decide without reinterpreting history |
| D6 | Refund under-payment **deferred**, but recorded precisely and a ticket created at closeout | most reversible | Whether a service fee is refundable is a **product** decision (most ticketing platforms do not refund fees) and this ticket must not answer it by accident. What is *not* deferred is stating the consequence exactly — see below |

#### A correction to the epic's readiness verdict, which I wrote wrongly

TKT-6's verdict says *"a refund returns the buyer's money — including passed-on fees — while the
settlement entries … are not reversed."* **That is wrong in the more dangerous direction.**
`refunds.go:176` computes `quantity × unit_amount` and never reads the total, so after this ticket a
refund returns **face value only** and the buyer is **under-refunded by the passed-on fees they
actually paid**. Not "fees are refunded but not settled" — fees are *not* returned at all.

That is a buyer-facing money defect, not a bookkeeping asymmetry, and it is the kind that arrives as
a chargeback. Deferred as a product decision (D6), stated here so nobody inherits my earlier wrong
sentence. The epic comment is being corrected too.

#### Introduced at plan-review, reviewed by no second model

**A1, A2, A3 — all three.** A1 is the consequential one: it adds a column, a backfill and a change to
two shipped exchange queries, on the judgement that an even exchange refunding the fee is a defect
rather than a deferred gap. If that judgement is wrong, the cost is a column nobody needed. If it is
right and I had deferred it, the cost is silent money movement on every exchange.

#### Test seam

`computeFeeBreakdown`, a new pure function beside the price consumer in `catalog_pricing.go` — the
same seam shape TKT-214 used, and the level where rounding and overflow are provable without HTTP or
PostgreSQL.

#### Pre-mortem

Applied at plan-review. Changed the plan in three places (A1, A2, A3).

#### Gate 2

Waived. Proceeding to `Building` with the six decisions and three unreviewed amendments named.

<!-- sdlc:stage=coding kind=summary -->
### Implementation — TKT-215

**Implemented by `main-agent` (Claude Opus 5)**, per `config.models.implement`. PR
[#175](https://github.com/mathd/ticketing_system/pull/175), branch `TKT-215-sale-charges-fees`,
3 commits, **+1530 / −34 across 17 files**.

```yaml
stage: coding
implementer: main-agent (Claude Opus 5)
pr: 175
commits: 3
diff: +1530/-34 (17 files)
gate_runs: 3 (2 red, distinct causes; 3rd green)
mutation_checks: 9
```

#### TDD

`computeFeeBreakdown` was **stubbed and the whole arithmetic suite observed red** — every rounding,
basis, incidence, null-winner and overflow case — before the logic existed. Restored, green.

**Nine mutation checks**, each killed by exactly the intended test and nothing else:

| Mutation | Killed by |
|---|---|
| round after multiplying (per-line instead of per-ticket) | `…RoundsPerTicket`, `…FloorsBeforeMultiplying` |
| absorbed fees added to the buyer total | `…SeparatesIncidence`, `TestComposedTotalAddsOnlyPassedOnFees` |
| a null winner treated as a zero fee | `…DistinguishesNullWinnerFromZeroFee` |
| a zero-amount winner dropped | `…ByBasis`, `…DistinguishesNullWinnerFromZeroFee` |
| fee failure degrading to "no fees" | **all 9** rows of the fail-closed matrix |
| channel dropped from the catalog request | `…SendsTheChannelToFeeResolution` |
| the contract's `not` clause removed | `…RefusesBothQuantityAndSeats/both_quantity_and_seats` |
| exchange source reading the gross total | `TestEvenExchangeOnAFeeCarryingOrderMovesNoMoney` |
| migration 0014's `Down` guard removed | `…DownRefusesToDestroyFeeComposition` |

The exchange one is the amendment's proof, and it reproduces the defect precisely:
`SourceTotal = 9400, want the face value 9100. Reading total_amount (9400) here makes an even
exchange look like a 300-cent downgrade.`

#### Two defects found by my own tests, not by review

1. **A `CHECK` constraint that accepted anything.** `jsonb_typeof(x -> 'resolution')` is SQL `NULL`
   when the key is missing, `NULL = 'object'` is `UNKNOWN`, and **a CHECK passes on UNKNOWN** — so
   the entire AND chain went unknown and an envelope with no resolution document at all was
   accepted. One `coalesce` per key fixes it. Three-valued logic in a constraint is the kind of thing
   that looks correct in review and is only ever caught by a test that tries the missing key.
2. **A smoke test that silently skipped.** It reads `COMMERCE_TEST_DATABASE_URL`; I had set
   `COMMERCE_MIGRATION_TEST_DATABASE_URL`. It printed `ok` while running **nothing**. Caught only
   because I grep for `RUN`/`PASS` lines rather than trusting `ok` — the same "silence is not
   success" trap that made me verify TKT-214's smoke tests too.

#### The fixture sweep, as a design consequence

`face_value_amount` is `NOT NULL` **with no default**, so **eight insert sites** had to state the
face value — three production paths and five test fixtures, plus a shared helper called at two
different schema versions.

A column default would have avoided all of it, and was rejected: there is no honest default (`0`
violates the bounds CHECK for any non-zero total, and "the total" is not expressible as one), and a
default would silently paper over an insert site that forgot — which is the exact bug the column
exists to prevent. The churn is the cost of the guarantee.

`seedV4Order` asks `information_schema` whether 0014 has been applied rather than assuming, because
two migration tests deliberately run against the **old** schema.

#### Gate

Three runs; the first two red with **distinct** causes, both mine:

1. `staticcheck SA4003` — an unreachable `total > math.MaxInt64` in `composedTotal`. `checkedAdd`
   already bounds at the contract cap, well below `MaxInt64`. Correct call: a check that cannot fire
   is not defence in depth.
2. `null value in column "face_value_amount"` across five smoke fixtures — the sweep above.

Third run green (`EXIT=0`, zero `Error|FAIL|drifted` lines in the body).

**Retro item, sharpened.** TKT-214's retro said *run module tests before the gate*; I did, and still
burned a gate run on **lint**. The rule is wider than I wrote it: run `golangci-lint` too. Both are
seconds; the gate is ~15 minutes. That is now three gate runs across two tickets lost to checks
available locally.

#### Deviations from the approved plan

None. The three plan-review amendments (A1 face value, A2 the `not` clause, A3 no channel to
inventory) were all implemented as specified. One thing the plan did not anticipate: the fixture
sweep's size, which followed from A1's column rather than from anything the plan got wrong.

**Reviewed by `gpt-5.6-luna` (Codex `adversarial-review`)**, per `config.models.aiReview`.

#### Why four passes, and why that is convergence rather than churn

The rule caps at two passes per *stable* diff, but resets when a pass invalidates the previous
pass's fix. That happened **twice**, and both times the new defect was created by my own fix:

- Pass 1's **F4** (make the exchange reversal fact use the gross) created pass 2's **F9** — the two
  journal legs stopped reconciling with what the provider actually moved.
- Pass 2's **F9** fix (sell target + carried fee) created pass 3's **F10** — the persisted
  replacement reservation then contradicted that journal.
- Pass 3's **F11** fix (checked arithmetic) created pass 4's **F14** — the new refusal ran *after*
  the hold was finalized, wedging capacity forever.

Each pass found a deeper defect at the root rather than re-litigating the last one. No finding was
resurfaced; none shrank into style.

#### Pass 1 — 7 findings, 6 `[high]`, all fixed

| # | Finding | Disposition |
|---|---|---|
| F1 | Percentage arithmetic **rejected valid fees** — and a test of mine asserted that rejection as required, pinning the bug | fixed: quotient/remainder decomposition |
| F2 | A valid rule whose arithmetic overflows left an **orphan hold** | fixed: validate before the hold |
| F3 | ADR-046 stated refunds return passed-on fees; **they do not** | fixed: the ADR now says so accurately |
| F4 | The exchange reversal fact recorded **face instead of gross** | fixed (and see F9) |
| F5 | A losing INSERT race quoted a total **never persisted**; `channel_code` missing from idempotency terms | fixed (and see F8) |
| F6 | A fee resolution for **another performance** was trusted | fixed: compared and failed closed |
| F7 | The migration accepted **contradictory** provenance | fixed: agreement enforced |

**F1 deserves emphasis.** The implementation was wrong *and my test defended it* — it asserted that
a large price at a 100% rate must be refused. A test can be wrong about what it wants, and then it
protects the defect from exactly the review that would have caught it.

**An existing test also caught me narrowing the system**: I had bounded fee arithmetic at catalog's
`Money` cap, but commerce's totals are bounded by int64 overflow.
`TestReserveOverflowGuardAppliesToResolvedAmount` exists to say *"the guard is about overflow, not
about large prices"* — and it failed, correctly.

#### Pass 2 — 2 `[high]`, both created by pass 1

**F8** — the lost-race branch returned 201 without checking the winner's *terms*. Two reserves under
one key with different channels both miss the lookup (the channel never reaches inventory), and the
loser was handed the winner's reservation as though its own terms had been accepted — then a retry
of that same request hit the replay path and got 409. One request succeeding once and conflicting
forever after. Fixed with a single `sameTerms` used by both paths, so they cannot disagree about
what "the same request" means.

**F9** — the journal asserted a refund that never happened: reversed 9400, sold 9100, provider delta
0. Fixed so the carried fee travels with the order and `sold − reversed == delta` **by
construction**.

#### Pass 3 — 3 findings, 2 created by pass 2

**F10** — the replacement reservation contradicted the journal, and a *second* exchange would have
lost the fee entirely. **F11** — `target + retainedFee` was unchecked and could wrap **negative
after the provider had already moved money**; my balance test accepted it, because two wrapped
int64s can differ by exactly the right amount.

**F12 `[medium]` — three of my tests admitted broken implementations**, all verified:

- the balance test passed an implementation reversing *face* and selling *target* (that balances too);
- the rate sweep gave **3997 of 4000 samples no expected value at all** — the int64 oracle skipped
  every sample whose product overflowed, which is nearly all of them. It looked thorough and checked
  almost nothing;
- the `sameTerms` channel case reused **one pointer on both sides**, so comparing pointer identity
  passed.

All three rebuilt with independent oracles (`big.Int`), distinct pointers, and the missing
seated-quantity case.

#### Pass 4 — 1 fixed, **1 rejected**

**F14 `[medium]` fixed** — the representability check ran *after* `transitionExchangeHold(finalize)`,
and finalizing removes the claim from the expiry predicate. An exchange that could never complete
would have withheld that capacity **forever** while every retry hit the same refusal. Moved ahead of
finalize, where a 409 costs nothing.

**F13 `[high]` REJECTED — not reachable.** It describes a retry straddling a deployment, where a
replacement row written by "the previous version" (bare target, no carried fee) survives
`ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING` while the journal uses the corrected gross. That previous version exists
**only inside this branch**: before migration 0014 there is no `face_value_amount` column at all, so
every shipped reservation has `gross == face` and a carried fee of **zero** — the old and new
computations agree exactly. The branch merges as one squash commit, so no deployment can sit between
the two behaviours. Recorded rather than fixed, because inventing a migration for a state that
cannot exist is worse than saying why it cannot.
